news.title: Susan Collins wins a seventh term in the US Senate, defeating Democrat Troy Jackson
news.description: Senator Susan Collins (R-ME) has been re-elected to a seventh term in the US Senate after a close race against Democratic challenger Troy Jackson. The incumbent won with 50% of the vote, while Jackson received 40% and independent candidate David Costello received 10%. This is the first time a Maine senator has won reelection with less than 50% of the vote since 1992. The campaign saw significant negative advertising, particularly against Collins, but she still maintained strong support in her home district. Her victory contributes to the overall trend of Democrats failing to flip seats in the 2026 elections.

news.title: Midterm elections head into the home stretch as candidates hit Labor Day events
news.description: Candidates in several states with competitive House and Senate races are beginning the stretch run of election season with Labor Day events at festivals, union halls and parades. This year’s campaigns already have been combative, busy and expensive. They are expected to get even more so as a larger number of voters tune in ahead of the Nov. 3 general election. The first statewide mail ballots already went out, in North Carolina, on Friday. Some of the busiest states are the handful with competitive Senate races, such as Maine, Ohio, Georgia and Michigan. Republicans control the chamber, but Democrats see a path to taking it back if they can flip four seats and hold on in competitive states where they hold a seat.

news.title: Senate, House candidates use Labor Day as kickoff for election final weeks
news.description: Candidates in several states with competitive House and Senate races are beginning the stretch run of election season with Labor Day events at festivals, union halls and parades. This year’s campaigns already have been combative, busy and expensive. They are expected to get even more so as a larger number of voters tune in ahead of the Nov. 3 general election. The first statewide mail ballots already went out, in North Carolina, on Friday. Some of the busiest states are the handful with competitive Senate races, such as Maine, Ohio, Georgia and Michigan. Republicans control the chamber, but Democrats see a path to taking it back if they can flip four seats and hold on in competitive states where they hold a seat.
